comparison: Both evaluations support the yoU-Net binarization tool's development and performance (C49-C50, C60-C61, C106, C123). OpenEval provides detailed validation metrics (97.1% for α-actinin-2, 60.4% for titin, 84.7% for myomesin), while peer reviewers affirm the tool 'appears promising' and 'outperforms Otsu thresholding.' Both agree the tool successfully addresses the binarization bottleneck.

Both evaluations strongly support sarcApp's comprehensive functionality (C9-C14, C51, C65-C67, C72-C73, C110-C111, C124, C126). OpenEval details the classification algorithms and customizable parameters, while peer reviewers describe it as 'an excellent software tool' that can 'automatically measure' multiple features 'quickly and accurately.' Both recognize the tool's value for multi-component sarcomere analysis.

Both evaluations support the Blebbistatin validation results (C91-C98, C100, C102). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative findings with statistical testing and orthogonal EM validation, while peer reviewers accept that 'sarcApp tool could capture changes in multiple features' and note consistency with previous studies. Both treat the validation as successful demonstration of sarcApp's functionality.

Both evaluations support the titin-specific Blebbistatin findings (C113-C119). OpenEval details the quantitative effects on doublet number/length and ring aspect ratio with statistical testing, while peer reviewers accept the tool's ability to 'quantify sarcomeres in titin and myomesin stained cardiomyocytes' without challenge. Both recognize differential effects across sarcomeric components.

Perfect agreement on myomesin M-Line quantification under Blebbistatin treatment (C128-C132). OpenEval provides detailed statistical analysis of reductions in myofibril number, M-Line number/length, and disorganized orientation. Peer reviewers accept these results as part of successful validation of sarcApp's multi-component analysis capabilities without objection.

Both evaluations support MYH6 knockdown findings (C138-C141). OpenEval notes no significant effects on structure lengths with one siRNA showing increased Z-Line number, while peer reviewers accept that 'neither MYH6 nor MYH7 knockdown perturbed the assembly of Z- or M-lines.' Both treat these results as supporting the broader conclusion about independent regulation.

Both evaluations support MYH7 knockdown findings (C143-C146). OpenEval details significant increases in Z-Line number with decreased length, no effect on titin doublets, but shortened M-Lines. Peer reviewers accept these differential effects as demonstrating 'different muscle myosins participate in sarcomere assembly in different manners.' Both recognize the distinction between β myosin II's roles.

Both evaluations support myomesin knockdown findings (C151-C158). OpenEval details no effect on Z-Line number or titin doublets but increased titin rings and reduced A-band organization. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'knockdown of MYOM perturbed the A-band/M-Line but not the Z-Line assembly.' Both treat these as key evidence for decoupled assembly mechanisms.

Both evaluations support the main biological conclusion about modular/decoupled sarcomere assembly (C16-C17, C52, C54, C147, C160). OpenEval emphasizes differential responses across perturbations and provides methodological recommendations. Peer reviewers accept that the analysis 'indicates that neither MYH6 nor MYH7 knockdown perturbed the assembly of Z- or M-lines' and acknowledge independent regulation without challenge.

OpenEval identifies consistent orientation findings across multiple markers (C77, C99-C101, C118, C132) as demonstrating sarcApp's novel orientation quantification capability. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this cross-marker consistency pattern, though individual results are accepted in other concordance records.

OpenEval rates titin localization observations and orientation model (C103-C105, C109) as UNCERTAIN, noting the mechanistic model is an inference requiring additional validation beyond antibody localization. Peer reviewers do not specifically evaluate these titin orientation claims.

OpenEval supports the methodology and bias minimization approach (C163-C165, C168-C169) as well-justified, though notes 'fully captures' variability is somewhat overstated. Peer reviewers do not specifically evaluate these methodological design claims.

OpenEval supports extensive background and context claims (C1-C6, C18-C32, C42-C43, C120, C133-C134, C136) as established knowledge with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers do not systematically evaluate these background claims, though R11 questions whether field limitations were overstated regarding existing tools.

OpenEval rates future impact and development claims (C55, C166-C167, C170-C174) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are forward-looking speculations rather than current results. Peer reviewers do not specifically evaluate these future-oriented claims.

Peer reviewers express UNCERTAIN evaluation of tool advantages (C40-C41), raising concerns about accessibility, robustness, and generalizability beyond one cell type and microscopy system. They note the binarization tool 'was not systematically compared with existing approaches.' OpenEval does not have a corresponding evaluation specifically addressing these limitation claims.

Peer reviewers express UNCERTAIN evaluation of claims about existing method limitations (C47-C48), noting surprise at no reference to SarcTrack (2019) which has 'exactly the same purpose,' suggesting authors may have overstated gaps in existing tools. OpenEval includes these claims in R13 as supported background but does not separately evaluate the characterization of field limitations.
